M5.L1.why: Exit Ticket: name the shaded fraction, partition a rectangle into thirds, find the fraction one 3-foot piece is of 12 feet of pipe.

M5.L2.why: Exit Ticket: circle the model showing 1 third, count equal parts, show garlic bread shared equally by 4 people.

M5.L3.why: Exit Ticket: count shaded sevenths, circle shapes in equal parts, fraction of a pizza each of 4 people gets.

M5.L4.why: Exit Ticket: partition shapes to show 1 fourth and 1 fifth, write the fraction for a shaded part.

M5.L5.why: Exit Ticket: partition identical rectangles 2 different ways into halves, thirds and fourths (equal shares need not have the same shape).

M5.L6.why: Exit Ticket: unit form and fraction form chart, write shaded fractions, draw fifths and eighths and explain why 1/5 is bigger than 1/8.

M5.L7.why: Exit Ticket: 2 fifths as a sum of unit fractions on a strip; fractions shaded and not shaded.

M5.L8.why: Exit Ticket: write unshaded fractions, sixths in 1 whole, label shaded and unshaded parts of a strip, fraction of a lawn mowed.

M5.L9.why: Exit Ticket: number bond of shaded and unshaded parts, each decomposed into unit fractions; draw a shape for a given bond.

M5.L10.why: Exit Ticket: build fractions greater than 1 from unit fractions (4 thirds). Grade 3 TEKS limit 3.3A and 3.3D to fractions up to 1, so nothing at grade level is assessed.

M5.L11.why: Exit Ticket: color one unit in fourths, thirds and halves strips, circle the largest and star the smallest; compare unit fractions with <, >, =.

M5.L12.why: Exit Ticket: fill in unit fractions to make comparisons true; 1/2 of a small carrot vs 1/4 of a large one, explain who ate more.

M5.L13.why: Exit Ticket: given a unit fraction shape, draw a possible whole; decide whose drawing of the whole is correct.

M5.L14.why: Exit Ticket: decide whose model correctly shows 2/3 shaded and explain (designating the whole).

M5.L15.why: Exit Ticket: number bond, partition a strip and label fractions on a 0–1 number line; share $1 equally among 5 students.

M5.L16.why: Exit Ticket: estimate and label fractions on a number line from 0 to 1, partition and place sixths.

M5.L17.why: Exit Ticket: label fractions on a number line from 0 to 2, write the wholes as fractions and box them (equivalence of whole numbers and fractions).

M5.L18.why: Exit Ticket: locate and label fractions on a number line; fraction of a gallon left over, shown on a number line.

M5.L19.why: Exit Ticket: place two fractions, circle the one closer to 0 and compare; decide whether 3/2 and 2/3 are the same with a number line.

M5.L20.why: Exit Ticket: place fourths on a number line, compare with >, <, =; is 2 wholes or 9/4 larger (distance from 0). Optional lesson.

M5.L21.why: Exit Ticket: label shaded fractions and circle the equal ones; draw 2 different representations of the same fraction.

M5.L22.why: Exit Ticket: use a number line and words to explain why 1 = 2/2 = 6/6.

M5.L23.why: Exit Ticket: draw two models of equivalent fractions and a number line that proves they are equal.

M5.L24.why: Exit Ticket: Henry ate 4/6 of a pie; what fraction in thirds ties him; number line and words.

M5.L25.why: Exit Ticket: number bond and number line in a given unit, rename 0 and 1 as fractions; how many copies of 1/4 make 1 whole.

M5.L26.why: Exit Ticket: label a whole-number fraction; partition 3 wholes into thirds and rename 3 as a fraction with a number line.

M5.L27.why: Exit Ticket: 2 yards of fabric cut into 1/5-yard pieces on a number line, how many pieces (2 = 10/5). Fifths are outside the Grade 3 denominators.

M5.L28.why: Exit Ticket: 2 thirds = __ twelfths, draw two models and explain why they are equal.

M5.L29.why: Exit Ticket: shade models to compare 2 thirds and 2 eighths and explain; circle the smaller of 3 sevenths and 3 fourths.

M5.L30.why: Exit Ticket: compare 3/9 and 3/5 with a symbol, then justify with two number lines.

M5.L31.why: No Exit Ticket sheet: the TE says to assess by observing students partition paper strips into equal parts with the lined-paper number line method.
